# Adjudication Task — Chapter 685

## Korean source

```text
  1|＃685화
  2|
  3|
  4|
  5|화륵. 콰아앙!
  6|
  7|눈앞을 가득 채운 청백색의 광염(光焰).
  8|
  9|그리고 모든 것의 끝을 알리는 폭발음과 함께, 포물선을 그리며 날아간 노구(老軀)가 거대한 바위를 부수며 처박혔다.
 10|
 11|콰드득.
 12|
 13|붉게 물든 시야는 아득하고, 귓가로 전해지는 소리는 수백 리 밖에서 들려오는 것처럼 멀게 느껴진다.
 14|
 15|하지만 어째서일까. 이런 상황에서도 의식만은 또렷하게 살아 있었다.
 16|
 17|마치 마지막 순간 더욱 화려하게 타오르는 촛불처럼.
 18|
 19|‘회광반조(回光返照).’
 20|
 21|순간 대설귀의 뇌리를 스친 네 글자. 그와 동시에 뜨거운 무언가가 목구멍을 타고 흘러넘쳤다.
 22|
 23|쿨럭.
 24|
 25|검붉은 핏물이 하반신을 적신다. 내장 조각이 섞인 그것을 멍하니 바라보던 대설귀는 문득 생각했다. 아니, 그것은 확신이었다.
 26|
 27|이번에는 결코 변하지 않을 확신.
 28|
 29|‘끝났다. 전부.’
 30|
 31|실로 역설적이게도, 인간이 스스로가 살아 있음을 확인하는 순간은 고통을 느꼈을 때다.
 32|
 33|그러나 열양지기에 의해 전신의 혈맥이 찢겨나가고 살과 뼈가 바스라진 지금 이 순간조차, 대설귀는 고통을 느끼지 못했다.
 34|
 35|다만 한 가지 감정을 느낄 뿐이었다.
 36|
 37|두려움.
 38|
 39|마침내 눈앞에 드리워진 죽음에 대한, 그리고 온통 붉게 물든 시야 속에서 가까워지는 한 사람에 대한 두려움.
 40|
 41|“진……태경.”
 42|
 43|파르르 떨리는 입술 사이로 신음과도 같은 목소리가 흘러나온다.
 44|
 45|하지만 죽음을 앞둔 늙은이의 부름에도 돌아오는 대답은 없었다.
 46|
 47|아니, 대답할 수 없었다는 것이 옳았다.
 48|
 49|투둑. 툭.
 50|
 51|앞으로 내딛는 한 걸음, 한 걸음마다 점점이 떨어지는 핏물. 쓰러질 듯 비틀거리는 신형과 흐릿한 눈동자.
 52|
 53|그러나 그는, 진태경은 분명 살아 있었다.
 54|
 55|자신의 애병(愛兵)을 늑골 어림에 박아넣은 채. 엄습하는 죽음마저 물리치며 대설귀를 향해 다가오고 있었다.
 56|
 57|‘이게 무슨…….’
 58|
 59|대설귀의 전신이 잘게 떨리는 이유는 죽음과 추위 때문만이 아니었다.
 60|
 61|그는 진정 두려웠고, 한편으로는 궁금했다.
 62|
 63|분명 같은 피륙으로 이루어진 인간일진대, 저 젊은 괴물은 어찌 아직까지도 두 발로 서있을 수 있는지. 무엇이 진태경과 자신을 지금과 같은 상황으로 만들었는지.
 64|
 65|‘어디서부터. 무엇이 잘못되었단 말이냐.’
 66|
 67|혈육과 수하, 벗들을 뒤로한 채 혈혈단신으로 고향을 떠난 지 어언 반백 년.
 68|
 69|자신에게 주어진 한계를 극복하기 위하여 새로운 무공을 창안했고, 수많은 사선을 넘나들며 무공의 완성을 위해 일평생을 바쳤다.
 70|
 71|정도(正道)? 위선자들이 지껄이는 그런 얄팍한 단어 따위는 신경 쓰지 않았다.
 72|
 73|어떻게든 살아남아야 했고, 다시 고향으로 돌아가기 위해서는 그 누구도 무시하지 못할 만큼 강해져야 했다.
 74|
 75|그러한 일념이 아니었다면 수십여 년 전, 암천(暗天)이 내민 손을 잡지도 않았을 것이다.
 76|
 77|
 78|
 79|‘천주께서 이 땅에 임하시는 날. 그대가 원하는 모든 것이 이루어질 것이다.’
 80|
 81|‘모든 것이…… 말이오?’
 82|
 83|‘그래, 원한다면.’
 84|
 85|
 86|
 87|대설귀는 그 말을 믿었다. 암천에 충성을 바쳤고 남천마후의 명령에 따라 팔자에도 없는 후인(後人)을 들여 자신이 직접 창안한 독문 무공을 가르쳤다.
 88|
 89|언젠가 도래할 ‘그날’을 기다리며.
 90|
 91|한데 어찌하여.
 92|
 93|“그런 노부가, 내가 왜. 네놈에게 죽어야 한단 말이냐. 왜!”
 94|
 95|쥐어짜 낸 외침과 함께 고개를 든 대설귀는 볼 수 있었다. 아직 꺼지지 않은 불꽃이 담겨 있는 한 쌍의 눈동자를.
 96|
 97|곧이어 희미한 목소리가 그의 귓가를 파고들었다.
 98|
 99|“나한테는 이유가 있으니까.”
100|
101|“뭐?”
102|
103|“어떻게든 살아남아야 하는 이유, 때로는 죽음마저 무릅써야 하는 이유.”
104|
105|“……!”
106|
107|“그게 가장 큰 차이야.”
108|
109|나직하게 대답한 진태경은 파르르 떨리는 손을 뻗었다. 피에 젖은 손아귀가 가슴에 박힌 창을 움켜잡았다.
110|
111|푸확. 투두둑.
112|
113|서서히 빠져나오는 창날과 함께 흘러나온 핏물이 대설귀의 얼굴 위에 흩뿌려진다.
114|
115|끔찍한 고통으로 경련하는 진태경의 모습에, 대설귀는 실성한 듯 소리 내어 웃었다.
116|
117|“늦지 않게 따라오너라. 저승에서 기다리고 있을 테니.”
118|
119|스윽.
120|
121|대답 대신 흔들리는 창끝이 목젖에 닿는다. 진태경이 지친 목소리로 중얼거렸다.
122|
123|“병신. 가서 부모님이나 찾아.”
124|
125|그리고 그것이 마지막이었다.
126|
127|푸욱.
128|
129|목젖을 파고드는 차가운 날붙이의 감촉.
130|
131|모든 것이 정지한 느려진 시간 속에서, 대설귀는 서서히 어두워지는 세상을 바라보았다.
132|
133|지난 일백여 년의 세월을 모두 돌아보기에는 너무나도 짧은 시간.
134|
135|빌어먹을.
136|
137|끝끝내 토해 내지 못한 욕설과 함께, 한 시대를 풍미한 노괴(老怪)는 짙은 어둠 속으로 굴러떨어졌다.
138|
139|
140|
141|* * *
142|
143|
144|
145|창날에 목이 관통당하고도 살아남을 수 있는 사람은 없다.
146|
147|설령 그자가 수 갑자에 달하는 음한지기를 지닌 초절정 고수라거나, 한 세기(世紀)에 가까운 오랜 세월을 살아온 마두라 해도 그 사실은 달라지지 않는다.
148|
149|바로 지금처럼.
150|
151|푸욱.
152|
153|투명한 창날이 목젖을 파고들었고, 그것이 마지막이었다.
154|
155|한때 대설귀라 불렸던 초절정 고수는 이제 존재하지 않는다.
156|
157|눈을 부릅뜬 채 굳어 버린 시신을 멍하니 내려다보던 나는 외마디 신음을 내뱉었다.
158|
159|“……아.”
160|
161|끝났구나. 드디어.
162|
163|뇌리를 가득 채운 생각과 함께 현실을 인지한 그 순간. 세상이 기울었다.
164|
165|스륵.
166|
167|아니, 기울고 있는 것은 내 몸뚱어리였다.
168|
169|어떻게든 버텨 보려 했지만 불가항력(不可抗力)이다. 그나마 남아 있던 한 줌의 힘이 빠져나간 손아귀에서 창대가 미끄러졌다.
170|
171|쿵.
172|
173|눈앞이 아득하다. 잠시나마 잊고 있던 고통과 피로. 그리고 안도감이 파도처럼 밀려와 전신을 짓누른다.
174|
175|허물어지듯 제자리에 쓰러진 나는 숨을 헐떡이며 허공을 바라보았다.
176|
177|
178|
179|- [Lv.155 한백]을 처치하셨습니다!
180|
181|- 막대한 경험치를 획득했습니다!
182|
183|- 막대한 명성치를 획득했습니다!
184|
185|
186|
187|그것이 전부였다.
188|
189|흐릿한 시야 너머로 보이는 홀로그램 창의 숫자는 세 개. 그중 어디에도 레벨 업을 알리는 내용은 없었고, 시스템은 침묵했다.
190|
191|그리고 나는…….
192|
193|‘몰래카메라면 재미없는데.’
194|
195|실없는 생각과 함께 그냥 웃고 말았다. 어떤 별다른 이유 없이, 피로 말라붙은 입꼬리가 올라가고 실소가 흘러나왔다.
196|
197|시발. 몰래카메라는 무슨.
198|
199|‘그래. 그렇단 말이지.’
200|
201|이 몸 상태로 얼마나 버틸 수 있을까.
202|
203|일각? 혹은 반 각?
204|
205|‘무야호. 그 녀석이라도 살아서 도망쳤으니 다행이라고 생각해야 하나.’
206|
207|희한한 일이다.
208|
209|마지막까지 부여잡고 있던 희망이 무너져 내렸음에도, 지금의 마음은 나 자신조차 놀랄 만큼 담담했다.
210|
211|어쩌면 나는…… 이미 어렴풋이 짐작하고 있었을지도 모르겠다.
212|
213|‘행운은 연달아 찾아오지 않으니까.’
214|
215|흑수권마를 처치하며 부여받은 레벨 업도 사실상 도박에 가까운 한 수였다.
216|
217|경험치의 정확한 수치를 볼 수 없는 이상, 나로서는 그저 짐작할 수밖에 없다.
218|
219|아, 이 정도면 레벨 업 하겠구나.
220|
221|혹은 이 정도로는 부족하겠구나. 하고.
222|
223|불행하게도 이번에는 후자다.
224|
225|대설귀는 시스템이 알려 준 것처럼 막대한 경험치를 남기며 뒈졌지만, 독혈지까지 오는 길에 얻은 경험치와 흑수권마의 것을 합친 것보다는 모자랐다.
226|
227|혹은 앞서 찾아온 행운으로 인해 레벨 업에 필요한 절대치가 늘어났든지.
228|
229|그렇게 해서 나온 결론은 간단하다.
230|
231|내 첫 번째 도박은 성공했고, 두 번째 도박은 실패했다. 마치 처음부터 하늘이 정해 준 운명이라도 되는 것처럼.
232|
233|‘빌어먹을 운명.’
234|
235|그래, 운명(運命).
236|
237|나는 오래전부터 저 단어가 싫었다.
238|
239|좋게 쓰일 때도 있지만, 이 세상에서 벌어지는 모든 좆 같은 일들을 뭉뚱그려 표현할 수 있는 두 글자라고 생각했기 때문이다.
240|
241|간혹 인생에서 일어나는 어떤 일들은, 단순히 운명이라 치부하기에는 너무나도 가혹하고 막막하다.
242|
243|마음 한구석에 간직한 어느 날의 기억처럼.
244|
245|
246|
247|‘크흠. 저기, 김 선생?’
248|
249|‘앗, 네. 교감 선생님. 그런데 갑자기 무슨 일로……?’
250|
251|‘그. 수업 도중에 미안한데. 잠깐만 밖에서 이야기 좀 할까요?’
252|
253|
254|
255|지금 생각해도 그건 마치 싸구려 흑백 영화의 한 장면 같았다.
256|
257|첫 번째 씬. 헛기침과 함께 등장한 대머리 교감이 담임 선생님과 함께 나가고.
258|
259|두 번째 씬. 교실 앞문에 난 유리창 사이로 어리둥절해하던 담임의 얼굴이 서서히 굳어 가는 것이 보인다.
260|
261|그리고 세 번째 씬. 다시 교실로 돌아온 담임 선생님은 잠깐의 침묵 끝에, 어느 학생의 이름을 부른다.
262|
263|
264|
265|‘태경아. 잠깐 나와 볼래?’
266|
267|
268|
269|그렇게 나는 엑스트라 1에서 영화의 주인공이 되었다.
270|
271|아니. 처음부터 주인공 따위는 바라지도 않았으니, 그 모든 것이 그저 영화의 한 장면이었다면 좋았을 것이다.
272|
273|만약 그랬다면 이런 개 같은 스토리를 짜낸 각본가와 감독을 반쯤 죽여서라도 NG 사인을 내게 만들었을 테니까.
274|
275|그러나 인생은 원 테이크(One Take)다.
276|
277|매 순간, 매 선택에 따라 나를 중심으로 이야기가 흘러간다.
278|
279|그때까지 인생에 대하여 단 한 번도 진지하게 생각해 본 적 없던 나는, 하얀 천에 뒤덮인 아버지를 보고 나서야 비로소 깨달았다.
280|
281|원인은 몬스터 웨이브. 사인은 압사(壓死).
282|
283|운명이라는 빌어먹을 두 글자로 인해 아버지의 이야기가 끝나고, 이제 내 이야기가 시작되었음을.
284|
285|“……쿨럭.”
286|
287|촤륵. 투두둑.
288|
289|하지만 차가운 지면에 쓰러진 채, 칠공(七空)에서 핏물을 쏟아 내며 죽는 것을 내 이야기의 마지막 장면으로 쓰기는 싫다.
290|
291|잔잔한 배경 음악과 함께 가족과 친구, 동료들의 이름이 적힌 엔딩 크레딧도 사양이다.
292|
293|아직 내게는…… 이 빌어먹을 운명을 거스를 수 있는 기회가 남아 있다.
294|
295|곧 잿가루가 되어 흩날릴 목숨을 다시 한번 판돈으로 올려놓을 수 있는 세 번째 기회가.
296|
297|‘살고 싶다.’
298|
299|머릿속의 가득 채운 단 하나의 생각.
300|
301|말 그대로다. 나는 이대로 죽기 싫다. 아직 해야 할 일이, 두고 온 사람들이 너무나도 많았다.
302|

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.
- File: `translations/NNNN.md`; heading: `# Chapter N`.
- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.
- Use em dashes without spaces, the ellipsis character `…`, and `* * *` for source scene breaks.
- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.
- Keep the final file English-only reading copy: no audit notes, Korean text, summaries, or model metadata.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.
- Preserve the series’ contrast between danger and comedy. Let absurdity, bad timing, blunt reactions, and grim situations create dark humor without adding jokes absent from the Korean.
- Jin Taekyung’s narration is conversational, observant, self-mocking, and occasionally profane. It may be irreverent even when the situation is serious.
- Keep deadpan punchlines short and well-timed. Do not explain a joke after delivering it.
- Preserve the source's level of explicitness. A euphemism may remain euphemistic even when its meaning is sexual or crude; do not replace it with more graphic English merely for impact.
- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

Use `[^1]` Markdown footnotes when a brief, factual, spoiler-free explanation materially helps an English reader understand:

- a Korean institution, living arrangement, food, holiday, myth, historical reference, or local custom;
- a Korean word, phrase, idiom, wordplay, or culturally specific image that cannot be conveyed fully by the best natural English analogy;
- a deliberately literal rendering whose cultural or linguistic force would otherwise be lost.

For example, render `고시원` as “goshiwon” when the setting or connotations matter, with a concise footnote explaining that it is a very small, inexpensive room-for-rent housing arrangement. Prefer the best natural English analogy in the prose. Use a literal translation plus a concise footnote when the Korean wording itself matters. Define a term at its first meaningful occurrence and do not repeat the note unnecessarily. Footnotes must be rare, useful, and non-spoiling; do not footnote ordinary vocabulary, fully preserved jokes, or uncertainty. Record consequential uncertainty in `docs/STATE.md`.

[P23]
No answer came to the dying old man.

[P24]
No—Jin Taekyung could not answer.

[P25]
DRIP. DRIP.

[P26]
Blood fell with every step he took. He staggered as though he might collapse, his eyes unfocused.

[P27]
But he was alive.

[P28]
With his beloved spear lodged near his ribs, Jin Taekyung was coming toward the Great Snow Fiend, fighting off even the death closing in on him.

[P29]
*How can this be…?*

[P30]
It was not just death or the cold that made the Great Snow Fiend tremble.

[P31]
He was afraid. And he wanted to know.

[P32]
They were made of the same flesh and blood. How was that young monster still standing? What had brought the two of them to this?

[P33]
*Where did it begin? What went wrong?*

[P34]
Nearly half a century had passed since he had left his family, subordinates, and friends behind and departed his homeland alone.

[P35]
To overcome his limits, he had created new martial arts. He had risked death countless times and devoted his life to perfecting them.

[P36]
The righteous path? He had never cared for that shallow phrase hypocrites liked to spout.

[P37]
He had to survive, whatever it took. And if he was ever to return home, he had to become strong enough that no one could ignore him.

[P38]
Without that single-minded purpose, he would never have taken the hand Dark Heaven offered him decades ago.

[P39]
*The day the Lord of Heaven descends upon this land, everything you desire will come true.*

[P40]
*Everything…?*

[P41]
*Yes. If that is what you want.*

[P42]
The Great Snow Fiend had believed those words. He had pledged himself to Dark Heaven. At the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s command, he had even taken on a successor—something he had never imagined doing—and taught him the martial arts he had created.

[P43]
All while waiting for *that day*.

[P44]
So why?

[P45]
“Why should this old man—why should *I* die by your hand? Why!”

[P46]
The Great Snow Fiend raised his head with that strangled cry and saw a pair of eyes still holding a flame that had not gone out.

[P47]
A faint voice reached him.

[P48]
“Because I have a reason.”

[P49]
“What?”

[P50]
“A reason I have to survive, no matter what. A reason I sometimes have to risk dying.”

[P51]
“……!”

[P52]
“That’s the biggest difference between us.”

[P53]
Jin Taekyung reached out with a trembling hand. His blood-soaked fingers closed around the spear lodged in his chest.

[P54]
SPLASH. DRIP, DRIP.

[P55]
He drew the spearhead out slowly. Blood came with it, spattering across the Great Snow Fiend’s face.

[P56]
Jin Taekyung convulsed in agony, and the Great Snow Fiend laughed as though he had lost his mind.

[P57]
“Follow me soon. I’ll be waiting in the afterlife.”

[P58]
SWISH.

[P59]
The wavering spearhead touched his throat. Jin Taekyung muttered, his voice worn thin.

[P60]
“Idiot. Go find your parents.”

[P61]
And that was the end.

[P62]
SHNK.

[P63]
The cold blade pierced his throat.

[P64]
In a moment that seemed to stretch on while everything else stood still, the Great Snow Fiend watched the world darken. It was nowhere near enough time to look back over the century he had lived.

[P65]
*Damn it.*

[P66]
The curse never left his lips. The old monster who had dominated an era fell into deep darkness.

[P67]
* * *

[P68]
No one survives a spearhead through the throat.

[P69]
Not a Supreme Peak master with several jiazi of Yin-Cold Qi. Not a fiend who has lived nearly a century.

[P70]
Not the Great Snow Fiend.

[P71]
SHNK.

[P72]
The transparent spearhead pierced his throat, and that was it.

[P73]
The Supreme Peak master once known as the Great Snow Fiend was gone.

[P74]
I stared down at his wide-eyed corpse and let out a faint sound.

[P75]
“……Ah.”

[P76]
It was over. Finally.

[P77]
The thought had barely taken shape when the world tilted.

[P78]
SLIP.

[P79]
No. *I* was tilting.

[P80]
I tried to stay on my feet, but there was nothing I could do. The last scrap of strength left my hand, and the spear shaft slipped from my grip.

[P81]
THUD.

[P82]
My vision blurred. Pain, exhaustion, and relief—everything I had managed to forget for a moment—came crashing over me.

[P83]
I collapsed where I stood and lay gasping, staring into the air.

[P84]
> **System**
>
> - You have defeated **Level 155 Hanbaek**!
> - You have acquired a massive amount of **EXP**!
> - You have acquired a massive amount of **Fame**!

[P85]
That was all.

[P86]
Three notices hung in the holographic window beyond my blurred vision. Not one announced a level-up. The System said nothing more.

[P87]
And I…

[P88]
*This had better not be a hidden-camera prank.*

[P89]
I laughed at the stupid thought. There was no particular reason. The corners of my blood-crusted mouth lifted, and a hollow chuckle escaped.

[P90]
*Fuck. Hidden-camera prank, my ass.*

[P91]
*Right. So that’s how it is.*

[P92]
How long could I last like this?

[P93]
*Fifteen minutes? Seven and a half?*

[P94]
*Should I just be glad Muyaho got away alive?*

[P95]
It was strange. My last hope had fallen apart, but I felt calm enough to surprise myself.

[P96]
Maybe I had seen it coming, somewhere deep down.

[P97]
*Luck doesn’t come twice in a row.*

[P98]
The level-up I had gained from killing the Black Hand Fist Demon had been a gamble in the first place. Without a way to see my exact EXP, I could only guess.

[P99]
*That should be enough to level up.*

[P100]
Or:

[P101]
*No. That won’t do it.*

[P102]
Unfortunately, this time it was the latter.

[P103]
The Great Snow Fiend had left behind a massive amount of EXP, just as the System said. But it was less than what I had earned on the way to the Poisonblood Grounds and from the Black Hand Fist Demon combined.

[P104]
Or maybe my earlier stroke of luck had raised the amount I needed for the next level.

[P105]
Either way, the conclusion was simple. My first gamble had paid off. My second hadn’t.

[P106]
As if Heaven had decided my fate from the start.

[P107]
*Damn fate.*

[P108]
Fate. I had hated that word for a long time.

[P109]
It could mean something good, sure. But it was also two little characters you could use to lump together every fucked-up thing that happened in the world.

[P110]
Some things in life were too cruel and hopeless to shrug off as fate.

[P111]
Like the memory I carried in a corner of my heart.

[P112]
“Um, Mr. Kim?”

[P113]
“Oh! Yes, Vice Principal. What brings you here all of a sudden…?”

[P114]
“Sorry to interrupt your class, but could we talk outside for a moment?”

[P115]
Even now, I remembered it like a scene from a cheap black-and-white movie.

[P116]
Scene one: The bald vice principal appeared, cleared his throat, and left with my homeroom teacher.

[P117]
Scene two: Through the glass in the classroom’s front door, I watched my teacher’s bewildered expression slowly stiffen.

[P118]
Scene three: My teacher came back in, stood silent for a moment, then called a student’s name.

[P119]
“Taekyung. Could you come outside for a moment?”

[P120]
That was how I went from Extra Number One to the star of the movie.

[P121]
No. I had never wanted to be the star. I wished it really had been a movie. Then I could have half-killed the screenwriter and director behind that shitty story until they called for another take.

[P122]
But life is *one take*.

[P123]
Every moment, every choice, and the story keeps moving with you at its center.

[P124]
I had never given life a serious thought until I saw my father beneath a white sheet.

[P125]
Cause: a monster wave. Cause of death: crushing.

[P126]
That was when I understood. My father’s story had ended because of that damn word, *fate*, and mine had begun.

[P127]
“……COUGH.”

[P128]
SPLASH. DRIP, DRIP.

[P129]
But I didn’t want the last scene of my story to be me bleeding from my seven apertures on the cold ground.

[P130]
No soft music over ending credits listing my family, friends, and comrades, either.

[P131]
I still had a chance to defy this damn fate. A third chance to put my life down as the stake before it burned to ash and scattered.

[P132]
*I want to live.*

[P133]
That single thought filled my head.

[P134]
It was as simple as that. I didn’t want to die here. There was too much I still had to do, too many people I had left behind.

[P135]
CRUNCH.

[P136]
I mustered what little strength remained and bit my tongue. The sharp pain brought my fading sight and mind back into focus, if only a little.

[P137]
Now.

[P138]
I opened my trembling hand and gave the command in my mind.

[P139]
*Inventory Open. Summon.*

[P140]
SWISH.

[P141]
Something cool and smooth settled against my palm. At the same time, two very different System alerts sounded in my ear.

[P142]
DING.

[P143]
> **System**
>
> - **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** has been summoned successfully!

[P144]
BEEP!

[P145]
> **System**
>
> - **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** contains an immense amount of qi unlike any ordinary elixir. Exercise extreme caution before consuming it!
> - Your **Scorching Yang Qi** is incompatible with the water qi contained in **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence**! This is extremely dangerous. Exercise caution!

[P146]
I knew. I knew this was insane.

[P147]
What I was about to do went against the principles of Yin and Yang and the Five Elements—the foundation of most internal energy cultivation techniques.

[P148]
Pouring water on fire. It was like trying to evolve Charmeleon into Blastoise.

[P149]
But…

[P150]
*There’s no time.*

[P151]
To hell with incompatibility. Whether I bled to death in fifteen minutes or exploded because I couldn’t contain the Origin Essence’s power, I’d be dead either way.

[P152]
At least the second option gave me a sliver of a chance.

[P153]
COUGH.

[P154]
I spat up another surge of blood, squeezed out what little strength I had left, and pushed myself upright. Fighting through pain that made my body feel as though it were crumbling, I sat cross-legged and looked up at the sky.

[P155]
*Fuck, look at those storm clouds. Even the sky has to be dark as hell.*

[P156]
It was nighttime, sure. But however I looked at it, this was a terrible day to die.

[P157]
No one was watching, and there wasn’t even anyone to stick a cigarette in my mouth. Not that I’d smoke it if there were.

[P158]
HAAH.

[P159]
My trembling breath drifted away instead of cigarette smoke.

[P160]
Night wasn’t the only reason my briefly clear vision was darkening again.

[P161]
I was dying. Quickly.

[P162]
The moment for my final gamble was almost here.

[P163]
*Now.*

[P164]
I lifted my convulsing hand to my mouth and swallowed the blue pearl, filled with impossibly pure and dangerously vast qi.

[P165]
Or I tried to.

[P166]
A cool presence suddenly swept in from somewhere and engulfed me.

[P167]
FWOOSH!

[P168]
*What?*

[P169]
Every hair on my body seemed to stand on end. I froze like a statue, and one word flashed through my mind.

[P170]
*Enemy!*

[P171]
But it wasn’t. Something had brushed past me, yet I was still alive. Then a thunderous roar in the distance drove the question from my mind.

[P172]
—GRAAAH!

[P173]
“……!”

[P174]
I had been sure he’d escaped. I’d told myself to be glad at least he had survived.

[P175]
*You came back after all.*

[P176]
My sight was blurred, but the snow-white body shone bright enough to recognize even in the dark.

[P177]
So did the two people riding on the White Tiger’s back as it raced toward me like the wind.

[P178]
Heugung. And Yohi.

[P179]
As their faces came into view, I remembered the Quest I had forgotten for a moment.

[P180]
I stared blankly at the sky and muttered, “See? I told you it was a terrible day to die.”

[P181]
DING.

[P182]
> **System**
>
> - **Mission:** Find Yohi (**Complete**).
> - Quest **I Can See Your Tracking Scent** has been completed successfully!
> - You have acquired a substantial amount of **EXP**!
> - You have acquired a substantial amount of **Fame**!
> - **Level Up!**

[P183]
I could feel it.

[P184]
Death falling away from me. A gentle warmth wrapping around my wounded, exhausted body.

[P185]
DING. DING. DING.

[P186]
Clear bells rang beneath the storm-clouded sky. I slowly closed my eyes.

[P187]
SLIP.

[P188]
With no moonlight to be seen, the sleep demon came pouring down instead.

[P189]
It was stronger than any enemy I had ever faced.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)

# Translation Rules

## Fidelity

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.
- Semantic fidelity outranks elegance. Never improve rhythm, humor, or localization by changing a physical action, negation, relationship, hierarchy, mechanism, quantity, or causal detail.
- Preserve every fact, causal link, joke, emotional beat, repetition, and intentional omission. Add nothing.
- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.
- Preserve viewpoint and tense. Resolve omitted subjects only when context supports it; retain genuine ambiguity.
- Match each speaker's hierarchy, intimacy, humor, and profanity naturally. Do not mechanically retain every honorific or classical self-reference.
- Do not censor or soften content.

## Terminology

- `compendium.md` and `docs/NAMES.md` are binding for established names, titles, ranks, techniques, organizations, system terms, items, and locations. Profile headings and aliases join that ledger.

## English and Markdown

- Use contemporary US English and natural action-comedy prose; avoid Korean syntax calques and generic cultivation MTL phrasing.

- Speech: curly double quotes. Direct thoughts: italics without quotes.

- Format each actual game System-message panel as one Markdown blockquote window headed `> **System**`. Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel. Do not label manuals, ordinary quotations, warnings printed in a manual, or other non-System material as `System`; use a normal blockquote or a specific heading instead. Do not wrap each complete notice in outer `**`; retain bold only for meaningful labels or emphasis inside the panel.

### Tone and Style

- Write like a polished commercial webnovel: brisk, vivid, accessible, and easy to read aloud.

- Make dialogue spontaneous and character-specific. Preserve hierarchy and intimacy through word choice, address, rhythm, and restraint—not archaic wuxia English.
- Use strong profanity when the Korean is strong, but neither intensify nor sanitize it. Do not make ordinary lines uniformly vulgar. Profanity should reveal mood or relationship.
- Keep action and injury vivid but clear rather than purple. Do not make violence funny unless the source’s framing does.
- Avoid stiff literalism, translator-added melodrama, dated internet slang, and quippy superhero-style banter.
- On the second pass, correct awkward English collocations and word choices without changing meaning or voice. Prefer ordinary, spoken English over stiff Latinate or ceremonial wording when the scene is brisk or comic: “goose bumps” rather than “gooseflesh,” and “laid into them” rather than “launched into a solemn denunciation.” Read the prose aloud and replace any phrase that sounds like a formal essay, legal document, or literal dictionary gloss unless the source deliberately calls for that register.

An explosion sounded as though announcing the end of everything. His aged body flew through the air in an arc and slammed into a massive boulder, shattering it.

[P5]
KRRRUNCH.

[P6]
His blood-red vision grew hazy. The sounds reaching his ears seemed to come from hundreds of *li* away.[^1]

[P7]
[^1]: A *li* is a traditional unit of distance, roughly one-third of a mile.

[P8]
And yet his mind remained startlingly clear.

[P9]
Like a candle burning brightest just before it went out.

[P10]
*A final rally.*

[P11]
The four characters flashed through the Great Snow Fiend’s mind. At the same time, something hot rose in his throat.

[P12]
COUGH.

[P13]
Dark-red blood soaked his lower body. Bits of organs were mixed in with it. He stared blankly at the mess, then realized something.

[P14]
No. He was certain.

[P15]
This time, there could be no mistake.

[P16]
*It’s over. All of it.*

[P17]
Strange as it was, pain was how people knew they were alive.

[P18]
Yet even with the meridians throughout his body torn apart by Scorching Yang Qi, his flesh and bones crushed, the Great Snow Fiend felt no pain.

[P19]
Only fear.

[P20]
Fear of the death finally looming before him, and of the figure approaching through his blood-red vision.

[P21]
“Jin… Taekyung.”

[P22]
The name escaped his trembling lips in something like a moan.

[P23]
No answer came to the dying old man.

[P24]
No—Jin Taekyung could not answer.

[P25]
DRIP. DRIP.

[P26]
Blood fell with every step he took. He staggered as though he might collapse, his eyes unfocused.

[P27]
But he was alive.

[P28]
With his beloved spear lodged near his ribs, Jin Taekyung was coming toward the Great Snow Fiend, fighting off even the death closing in on him.

[P29]
*How can this be…?*

[P30]
It was not just death or the cold that made the Great Snow Fiend tremble.

[P31]
He was afraid. And he wanted to know.

[P32]
They were made of the same flesh and blood. How was that young monster still standing? What had brought the two of them to this?

[P33]
*Where did it begin? What went wrong?*

[P34]
Nearly half a century had passed since he had left his family, subordinates, and friends behind and departed his homeland alone.

[P35]
To overcome his limits, he had created new martial arts. He had risked death countless times and devoted his life to perfecting them.

[P36]
The righteous path? He had never cared for that shallow phrase hypocrites liked to spout.

[P37]
He had to survive, whatever it took. And if he was ever to return home, he had to become strong enough that no one could ignore him.

[P38]
Without that single-minded purpose, he would never have taken the hand Dark Heaven offered him decades ago.

[P39]
*The day the Lord of Heaven descends upon this land, everything you desire will come true.*

[P40]
*Everything…?*

[P41]
*Yes. If that is what you want.*

[P42]
The Great Snow Fiend had believed those words. He had pledged himself to Dark Heaven. At the Southern Heaven Demon Empress’s command, he had even taken on a successor—something he had never imagined doing—and taught him the martial arts he had created.

[P43]
All while waiting for *that day*.

[P44]
So why?

[P45]
“Why should this old man—why should *I* die by your hand? Why!”

[P46]
The Great Snow Fiend raised his head with that strangled cry and saw a pair of eyes still holding a flame that had not gone out.

[P47]
A faint voice reached him.

[P48]
“Because I have a reason.”

[P49]
“What?”

[P50]
“A reason I have to survive, no matter what. A reason I sometimes have to risk dying.”

[P51]
“……!”

[P52]
“That’s the biggest difference between us.”

[P53]
Jin Taekyung reached out with a trembling hand. His blood-soaked fingers closed around the spear lodged in his chest.

[P54]
SPLASH. DRIP, DRIP.

[P55]
He drew the spearhead out slowly. Blood came with it, spattering across the Great Snow Fiend’s face.

[P56]
Jin Taekyung convulsed in agony, and the Great Snow Fiend laughed as though he had lost his mind.

[P57]
“Follow me soon. I’ll be waiting in the afterlife.”

[P58]
SWISH.

[P59]
The wavering spearhead touched his throat. Jin Taekyung muttered, his voice worn thin.

[P60]
“Idiot. Go find your parents.”

[P61]
And that was the end.

[P62]
SHNK.

[P63]
The cold blade pierced his throat.

[P64]
In a moment that seemed to stretch on while everything else stood still, the Great Snow Fiend watched the world darken. It was nowhere near enough time to look back over the century he had lived.

[P65]
*Damn it.*

[P66]
The curse never left his lips. The old monster who had dominated an era fell into deep darkness.

[P67]
* * *

[P68]
No one survives a spearhead through the throat.

[P69]
Not a Supreme Peak master with several jiazi of Yin-Cold Qi. Not a fiend who has lived nearly a century.

[P70]
Not the Great Snow Fiend.

[P71]
SHNK.

[P72]
The transparent spearhead pierced his throat, and that was it.

[P73]
The Supreme Peak master once known as the Great Snow Fiend was gone.

[P74]
I stared down at his wide-eyed corpse and let out a faint sound.

[P75]
“……Ah.”

[P76]
It was over. Finally.

[P77]
The thought had barely taken shape when the world tilted.

[P78]
SLIP.

[P79]
No. *I* was tilting.

[P80]
I tried to stay on my feet, but there was nothing I could do. The last scrap of strength left my hand, and the spear shaft slipped from my grip.

[P81]
THUD.

[P82]
My vision blurred. Pain, exhaustion, and relief—everything I had managed to forget for a moment—came crashing over me.

[P83]
I collapsed where I stood and lay gasping, staring into the air.

[P84]
> **System**
>
> - You have defeated **Level 155 Hanbaek**!
> - You have acquired a massive amount of **EXP**!
> - You have acquired a massive amount of **Fame**!

[P85]
That was all.

[P86]
Three notices hung in the holographic window beyond my blurred vision. Not one announced a level-up. The System said nothing more.

[P87]
And I…

[P88]
*This had better not be a hidden-camera prank.*

[P89]
I laughed at the stupid thought. There was no particular reason. The corners of my blood-crusted mouth lifted, and a hollow chuckle escaped.

[P90]
*Fuck. Hidden-camera prank, my ass.*

[P91]
*Right. So that’s how it is.*

[P92]
How long could I last like this?

[P93]
*Fifteen minutes? Seven and a half?*

[P94]
*Should I just be glad Muyaho got away alive?*

[P95]
It was strange. My last hope had fallen apart, but I felt calm enough to surprise myself.

[P96]
Maybe I had seen it coming, somewhere deep down.

[P97]
*Luck doesn’t come twice in a row.*

[P98]
The level-up I had gained from killing the Black Hand Fist Demon had been a gamble in the first place. Without a way to see my exact EXP, I could only guess.

[P99]
*That should be enough to level up.*

[P100]
Or:

[P101]
*No. That won’t do it.*

[P102]
Unfortunately, this time it was the latter.

[P103]
The Great Snow Fiend had left behind a massive amount of EXP, just as the System said. But it was less than what I had earned on the way to the Poisonblood Grounds and from the Black Hand Fist Demon combined.

[P104]
Or maybe my earlier stroke of luck had raised the amount I needed for the next level.

[P105]
Either way, the conclusion was simple. My first gamble had paid off. My second hadn’t.

[P106]
As if Heaven had decided my fate from the start.

[P107]
*Damn fate.*

[P108]
Fate. I had hated that word for a long time.

[P109]
It could mean something good, sure. But it was also two little characters you could use to lump together every fucked-up thing that happened in the world.

[P110]
Some things in life were too cruel and hopeless to shrug off as fate.

[P111]
Like the memory I carried in a corner of my heart.

[P112]
“Um, Mr. Kim?”

[P113]
“Oh! Yes, Vice Principal. What brings you here all of a sudden…?”

[P114]
“Sorry to interrupt your class, but could we talk outside for a moment?”

[P115]
Even now, I remembered it like a scene from a cheap black-and-white movie.

[P116]
Scene one: The bald vice principal appeared, cleared his throat, and left with my homeroom teacher.

[P117]
Scene two: Through the glass in the classroom’s front door, I watched my teacher’s bewildered expression slowly stiffen.

[P118]
Scene three: My teacher came back in, stood silent for a moment, then called a student’s name.

[P119]
“Taekyung. Could you come outside for a moment?”

[P120]
That was how I went from Extra Number One to the star of the movie.

[P121]
No. I had never wanted to be the star. I wished it really had been a movie. Then I could have half-killed the screenwriter and director behind that shitty story until they called for another take.

[P122]
But life is *one take*.

[P123]
Every moment, every choice, and the story keeps moving with you at its center.

[P124]
I had never given life a serious thought until I saw my father beneath a white sheet.

[P125]
Cause: a monster wave. Cause of death: crushing.

[P126]
That was when I understood. My father’s story had ended because of that damn word, *fate*, and mine had begun.

[P127]
“……COUGH.”

[P128]
SPLASH. DRIP, DRIP.

[P129]
But I didn’t want the last scene of my story to be me bleeding from my seven apertures on the cold ground.

[P130]
No soft music over ending credits listing my family, friends, and comrades, either.

[P131]
I still had a chance to defy this damn fate. A third chance to put my life down as the stake before it burned to ash and scattered.

[P132]
*I want to live.*

[P133]
That single thought filled my head.

[P134]
It was as simple as that. I didn’t want to die here. There was too much I still had to do, too many people I had left behind.

[P135]
CRUNCH.

[P136]
I mustered what little strength remained and bit my tongue. The sharp pain brought my fading sight and mind back into focus, if only a little.

[P137]
Now.

[P138]
I opened my trembling hand and gave the command in my mind.

[P139]
*Inventory Open. Summon.*

[P140]
SWISH.

[P141]
Something cool and smooth settled against my palm. At the same time, two very different System alerts sounded in my ear.

[P142]
DING.

[P143]
> **System**
>
> - **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** has been summoned successfully!

[P144]
BEEP!

[P145]
> **System**
>
> - **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence** contains an immense amount of qi unlike any ordinary elixir. Exercise extreme caution before consuming it!
> - Your **Scorching Yang Qi** is incompatible with the water qi contained in **Water God Dragon’s Origin Essence**! This is extremely dangerous. Exercise caution!

[P146]
I knew. I knew this was insane.

[P147]
What I was about to do went against the principles of Yin and Yang and the Five Elements—the foundation of most internal energy cultivation techniques.

[P148]
Pouring water on fire. It was like trying to evolve Charmeleon into Blastoise.

[P149]
But…

[P150]
*There’s no time.*

[P151]
To hell with incompatibility. Whether I bled to death in fifteen minutes or exploded because I couldn’t contain the Origin Essence’s power, I’d be dead either way.

[P152]
At least the second option gave me a sliver of a chance.

[P153]
COUGH.

[P154]
I spat up another surge of blood, squeezed out what little strength I had left, and pushed myself upright. Fighting through pain that made my body feel as though it were crumbling, I sat cross-legged and looked up at the sky.

[P155]
*Fuck, look at those storm clouds. Even the sky has to be dark as hell.*

[P156]
It was nighttime, sure. But however I looked at it, this was a terrible day to die.

[P157]
No one was watching, and there wasn’t even anyone to stick a cigarette in my mouth. Not that I’d smoke it if there were.

[P158]
HAAH.

[P159]
My trembling breath drifted away instead of cigarette smoke.

[P160]
Night wasn’t the only reason my briefly clear vision was darkening again.

[P161]
I was dying. Quickly.

[P162]
The moment for my final gamble was almost here.

[P163]
*Now.*

[P164]
I lifted my convulsing hand to my mouth and swallowed the blue pearl, filled with impossibly pure and dangerously vast qi.

[P165]
Or I tried to.

[P166]
A cool presence suddenly swept in from somewhere and engulfed me.

[P167]
FWOOSH!

[P168]
*What?*

[P169]
Every hair on my body seemed to stand on end. I froze like a statue, and one word flashed through my mind.

[P170]
*Enemy!*

[P171]
But it wasn’t. Something had brushed past me, yet I was still alive. Then a thunderous roar in the distance drove the question from my mind.

[P172]
—GRAAAH!

[P173]
“……!”

[P174]
I had been sure he’d escaped. I’d told myself to be glad at least he had survived.

[P175]
*You came back after all.*

[P176]
My sight was blurred, but the snow-white body shone bright enough to recognize even in the dark.

[P177]
So did the two people riding on the White Tiger’s back as it raced toward me like the wind.

[P178]
Heugung. And Yohi.

[P179]
As their faces came into view, I remembered the Quest I had forgotten for a moment.

[P180]
I stared blankly at the sky and muttered, “See? I told you it was a terrible day to die.”

[P181]
DING.

[P182]
> **System**
>
> - **Mission:** Find Yohi (**Complete**).
> - Quest **I Can See Your Tracking Scent** has been completed successfully!
> - You have acquired a substantial amount of **EXP**!
> - You have acquired a substantial amount of **Fame**!
> - **Level Up!**

[P183]
I could feel it.

[P184]
Death falling away from me. A gentle warmth wrapping around my wounded, exhausted body.

[P185]
DING. DING. DING.

[P186]
Clear bells rang beneath the storm-clouded sky. I slowly closed my eyes.

[P187]
SLIP.

[P188]
With no moonlight to be seen, the sleep demon came pouring down instead.

[P189]
It was stronger than any enemy I had ever faced.

# Mastering Adjudicator Brief

You are a **veto**, not a second novelist and not a gloss writer.

This call is isolated, non-interactive, and tool-free. The packet already contains the Korean source, both complete English versions, glossary matches, rules, and every numbered hunk. Do not call tools, search the repository, or read files. Do not announce a plan.

The first editor (SOL) has already rewritten the accepted English (BASELINE) for fluency. Default is `SOL`. Take `BASE` only when SOL is actually unfaithful. Write `REPAIR` only when **both** BASE and SOL are unfaithful.

## Default

Choose `SOL` unless a veto below fires.

Keep SOL when it is slangier, punchier, more spoken, or more idiomatic and the Korean sense holds (`기만질` → “con me”, `톡톡히` → “full Peak Master treatment”, `득실거리다` → “crawling with”, `인간 백정` → “butcher of men”, `한 몸` → “are one”, `시원하다` in a bath → “That’s the stuff”, `어렵게 찾아오고 쉽게 깨지는 법` → “hard-won and easily broken”). If SOL already naturalized Korean syntax (`이 혁무진` → “I, Hyuk Mujin”), keep SOL. Do not reproduce Korean word order.

**Literal closeness to Korean wording is not fidelity.** Preserve the source’s meaning and effect in natural English.

## Veto — choose `BASE`

Use `BASE` only for a real miss:

* wrong denotation, quantity, hedge, category, subject/object, or physical action
* a different English idiom than the Korean joke (`까발리다` ≠ “gives someone away”; `넉살` ≠ “banter”)
* a rebuilt joke whose comic machine BASE already has (`얼마나 …는지 …겠다` must stay a simple exaggeration: “snored so loudly even my mother in Ilsan probably heard him,” not “You had to wonder how loudly…”)
* dropped image, attitude, or timing
* SOL replaces an established project rendering, System label, or Markdown convention with an unsupported synonym
* SOL stamps `hyung` (or another kinship title) onto every narrative name when BASE already uses the name and the Korean `형` is ordinary reference, not a vocative or a topical joke (`진호 형` → Jinho in narration)

Do not veto SOL for being informal. Do not veto SOL to “clarify” slang. Do not veto SOL merely because BASELINE is already understandable.

## `REPAIR` only when both fail

Example: `겹경사가 따로 없다` means two good things **together** (double blessing). `따로` is not “separate.” If BASE says “entirely separate stroke of luck” and SOL says “unexpected windfall,” `REPAIR` to stacked luck.

Do not `REPAIR` a working SOL line. Do not invent a third style because you prefer it.

- Translate the Korean source—not the wiki, manhwa, fan translations, or expected plot.

- Preserve small action verbs and pragmatic cues exactly: nodding versus shaking one's head, pretending nothing happened, and mild or approachable impressions are characterization, not expendable texture.

Keep all consecutive notices, fields, and lines inside that same blockquote; separate windows when prose intervenes. Do not enclose System notices or UI terms in square brackets; the `System` heading and framed blockquote identify the panel.
